candidates.title: 'Our costs went up' has stopped working: when everyone gives the same reason for a price rise, customers hear an excuse (field study 2026 + classic fairness study 1986 + this week's wave of cost-based price hikes)

sources.publisher: Inside Retail US, republished from The Conversation (Hoorsana Damavandi, U. Tennessee; Kersi D. Antia, Ivey; Praveen K. Kopalle, Dartmouth)
sources.claim: Field study with a Canadian self-storage company that randomly gave customers one of three price-hike justifications: cost-based and quality-based reasons produced no measurable change in churn vs no justification; the market-based reason (supply, demand, scarcity) made customers 30% less likely to exit. Authors: 'In times of prolonged inflation, like today, cost-based justifications may not be seen as fair anymore'; when every company cites higher costs, customers read it as an excuse. Sample size and journal not stated in the article.

sources.publisher: American Economic Review 76(4) (Kahneman, Knetsch, Thaler, 'Fairness as a Constraint on Profit Seeking')
sources.claim: Snow shovel $15 -> $20 the morning after a snowstorm: 82% unfair (N=107). Grocer raises lettuce 30 cents after the wholesale price rose due to a shortage: 79% acceptable (N=101). Dual entitlement: customers are entitled to the reference terms, firms to their reference profit.

sources.publisher: Reynolds Consumer Products Q3 2026 results (SEC 8-K exhibit 99.1)
sources.claim: Q3 2026: price +9%, retail volume -7%, net revenue +1%; CEO: 'acting decisively to address significant commodity inflation'. (Volume fall is not attributable to messaging; do not imply causation.)

sources.publisher: Daily Caller (summarising earnings releases; WSJ for Kraft Heinz quote)
sources.claim: Household brands (Reynolds, Kraft Heinz, Clorox, P&G) all cite higher commodity/fuel/transport costs in early-November results; Kraft Heinz CEO says more increases likely in 2027. Used only as a spark showing everyone gives the same reason; primary figure verified via Reynolds 8-K.
After CEO talk of testing dynamic pricing on new digital menu boards, backlash compared it to Uber surge pricing; Wendy's: 'Wendy's will not implement surge pricing.'

sources.publisher: Futurism (Victor Tangermann), citing PCMag, Washington Post, Reddit
sources.claim: Starlink 'demand surcharges' for high-demand areas, reported up to $1,500 in parts of Alaska (June 2026, per PCMag); customers describe them as opaque and hard to contest.

candidates.claim: The reason you give for a price rise changes how customers judge it (1986: same kind of rise, 82% unfair vs 79% acceptable depending on reason). But in prolonged inflation, the generic cost reason no longer reduced churn in a 2026 field study; a specific, market-based reason did (-30% exits). My take: a reason works only when it is specific and checkable, not when it is the line everyone uses.

gates.brand_fit: pass: strategist voice on pricing communication; every SMB owner raises prices
gates.story: strongest: tension 'the fairest-sounding reason is the one that no longer works'; concrete image: snow shovel vs lettuce; the same note on every price tag
gates.repeat_7d: pass with care: 11-03 was price memory (which prices customers remember); this is how to explain a rise. Different angle, flag in framing note
gates.bilingual: pass: inflation is universal; especially sharp for the Persian audience living with long inflation

lenses.red_team: Single field study, single company (self-storage), sample size and journal not given in the article: say 'one field study' and keep caveat. Market-based reasons (demand/scarcity) look like they contradict Kahneman's snow shovel (demand-driven rises judged unfair): reconcile honestly: in 1986 a cost reason was accepted; in long inflation the generic cost reason lost force; the self-storage 'scarcity' was concrete and true. Never advise inventing scarcity. Reynolds 7% volume fall is not caused by messaging: use only '+9% price, citing commodity inflation' as an example of the common line, or skip numbers. Wendy's never implemented surge pricing: say 'just the word surge caused backlash'. 'My take' for the synthesis.
lenses.audience_psychology: Dual entitlement / reference price; persuasion knowledge: a repeated line becomes a recognised tactic and loses meaning; specificity as a credibility signal; habituation.
lenses.brand_fit: Practical, non-preachy, ethical: honesty + specificity; gives owners a usable template ('what changed, by how much, what you did first').

pick_reason: Highest total (93) and strongest story gate: a counter-intuitive tension (the reason that sounds fairest has stopped working) with concrete images (snow shovel vs lettuce; the same note on every price tag). Direct, daily utility for every business owner; extremely relevant to a Persian audience living through long inflation and to an international audience facing this week's wave of cost-based price hikes. Evergreen core (1986) + 2026 field study + Nov 4-6 spark. Different angle from 11-03 (which prices customers remember).
scores_note: growth, reach, qualified-follower, regional, psychology, utility and originality are estimates; verifiability and freshness are judged from sources.
